text:
sasha: Heads-up, noticed a perf regression in prefix cache hit-rate after the kernel-selection swap on canary. overall tail latency up ~12% during small deploy waves. graph: https://internal.grafana/redwood/d/abc123/prefix-cache

kai: ack. timeline? which kernel and which deploy wave?

sasha: changed kernel selector to prefer kernel-v2 for small-seq workloads (experiment 1.3). regression appeared right after autoscaler spike at 03:07 UTC when a burst added ephemeral pods. hit-rate dropped from ~78% -> ~41% for 0-8 token prefixes.

maria: interesting — early note: kernel-v2 changed batching boundaries (coarser token grouping) which altered the exact prefix keys we compute for KV cache. if keys include token-boundary metadata we may be generating different keys for the same logical prefix.

kai: can you paste the keying logic we use in the runtime? small snippet?

maria: sure — simplified version we ship in runtime: 

```python
def make_cache_key(model, prompt_prefix, seq_info):
    # seq_info used to encode token boundaries (kernel preference)
    return f"{model}:{seq_info}:{prefix_hash(prompt_prefix)}"
```

maria: kernel-v2 started adding `seq_info` that included chunking mode (`grp_64` vs `grp_128`). so identical prompt_prefix ended up with different cache keys depending on which kernel path served it.

sasha: that seems like the main root cause. also saw TTL churn: deploy-time warmers seed keys with TTL=30m, but autoscaler hook launches and the new pod's local eviction policy is LRU with a small in-mem window, so between warmers completing and traffic spiking some keys get evicted. combined with key-diffing -> misses.

devbot: perf-regression-bot: flagged alert prefix-cache-hit-rate < 50% for service/runtime-canary at 2026-03-04T03:12:07Z

rachel: summary of impacts observed in canary: higher token cost, more KV misses -> more compute calls -> queueing -> some 503s on the tail. customer-facing latency SLOs borderline for short chat flows.

kai: proposed fixes (short):
- normalize keying: remove kernel-specific seq_info from cache key; move kernel metadata to routing tag not key.
- canonicalize prompt_prefix (lowercase, collapse whitespace, normalize punctuation).
- change prewarmer TTL to 2h for critical prefixes and use autoscaler lifecycle hook to mark prefilled pods as sticky for 15m.
- add scheduled background seeder that synthesizes high-entropy prefixes (entropy > threshold) instead of relying solely on historical top-k.

maria: + add a small deterministic hash version in front of the key so we don't leak long prefix strings into the keyspace and to make eviction patterns more uniform. sample normalization: 

```python
import re, hashlib

def normalize_prefix(p):
    p2 = re.sub(r"\s+"," ", p.strip().lower())
    p2 = re.sub(r"[\u2000-\u206F]","", p2)  # strip weird unicode punctuation
    return p2

def cache_key(model, prefix):
    p = normalize_prefix(prefix)
    return f"{model}:{hashlib.sha1(p.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]}"
```

kai: also suggests adding a small metric split by token-length bucket (0-4,5-8,9-16,>16) and by kernel path so we can see if a kernel selection flip rekeys traffic. here's a quick query to compute hit-rate from kcache metrics: 

```sql
SELECT bucket, kernel_path, sum(hit) / count(*) as hit_rate
FROM prefix_cache_logs
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY bucket, kernel_path
ORDER BY bucket;
```

sasha: good. i'll run that and schedule a 30m experiment: 1) revert kernel selector for canary -> measure hit-rate, 2) apply key-normalization hotfix (no seq_info) on a small subset, 3) run synthetic seeder for high-entropy prefixes for 1h.

maria: one thing to watch: synthetic traffic should use the same tokenization pipeline as live traffic. if we generate by char-level heuristics we won't hit tokenization boundaries that matter. the seeder job should call our tokenizer endpoint or use the same lib.

rachel: ops Q: can the autoscaler annotate spawned pods so prewarmer jobs can target them? if so we can make prewarmer attach to pod label for a short handshake window.

kai: yes, autoscaler can add label `prefilled=true` on lifecycle hook and prewarmer controller can target pods with that label. also add a TTL label with epoch so we can garbage-collect stale prewarms.

devbot: todo created: ENGRT-1412 - run canary rollback + normalization experiment (owner: sasha, due: 2026-03-04T08:00Z)

sasha: i'll post results in this thread after the run. priority P0 for the canary lane until we confirm hit-rate back to baseline.

maria: one more perf note: batching heuristics in kernel-v2 coalesced small requests into a larger batch which increased queueing for tiny-latency flows. even if we fix keying we may want a prefer-latency tag to force smaller batches for the chat-short route.

kai: agreed. action items: 
- sasha: run SQL + rollback test + post metrics (ETA 2h)
- maria: prepare normalization PR + unit tests for tokenizer equivalence (ETA 6h)
- ops: implement autoscaler label handshake (ETA 24h)

rachel: thanks team. :thumbsup:

sasha: thanks — will update.\/end of thread
